I Held My Father's Hand While the Dialysis Machine Beeped. Now My Doctor Wants Me on the Same Pills That Put Him There.
At 3:47 AM I Sat at My Kitchen Table Googling "Metformin Side Effects Lactic Acidosis" While My Unfilled Prescription Mocked Me From the Counter.
My father died at 68.
I'm 59.
Three weeks ago, my doctor closed the exam room door.
The click echoed.
She sat down. Pulled up my chart without looking at me.
"Sandra. We can't wait anymore. I'm prescribing Metformin. 500 milligrams twice daily. You'll start today."
My throat constricted. The walls tilted.
Metformin.
The same medication they gave my father. Eleven years of it.
His stomach first - cramping so bad he'd double over in the grocery store, sweating through his shirt.
Then the diarrhea. Accidents in public. Adult diapers by month eight. Just staying home. Every day. Afraid to leave the house.
The afternoon my father stood up from the dinner table - dizzy - and his legs just buckled.
Face-first into the coffee table. Blood streaming from where his forehead split open. Six stitches.
The kidney function tests that got worse. And worse. And worse.
Creatinine climbing. GFR dropping. Year 8: Stage 3 kidney disease. Year 10: Stage 4.
Year 11: Dialysis three times a week. His arm with the fistula. Swollen. Purple. Painful.
A man who used to run marathons couldn't walk to the mailbox without gasping for breath.
My mother's words at the funeral, barely audible over my own sobs: "The pills didn't save him. They just made him suffer longer."
Eleven years of medication.
Eleven years of side effects.
My father died anyway. Heart failure. In his sleep. The Metformin controlled his blood sugar. Didn't save his kidneys. Didn't prevent his death.
I sat in my car in the parking lot. Couldn't turn the key. Just gripped the steering wheel.
The prescription crinkled in my jacket pocket. I pulled it out. Stared at it.
Metformin 500mg. Take one tablet twice daily.
My hands shook.
My husband was unloading groceries when I walked through the door. "Hey. How was your checkup?"
The words stuck. I handed him the prescription without speaking.
A1C 8.2.
The grocery bag hit the floor. Eggs shattered. Milk carton split. He didn't notice. Both hands covered his mouth. Tears streaming down his face.
"No." His voice broke. "Sandra, I watched what that medication did to your father. I can't. I can't watch you go through that. I can't—"
He couldn't finish. Turned away. Shoulders shaking.
That night I lay awake. The ceiling fan rotated. Over. And over. And over.
Red numbers glowed on the clock: 11:52 PM.
Rolled over. 12:41 AM.
Again. 1:38 AM.
At 2:23 AM I gave up. Went downstairs. Sat at the kitchen table. Opened my laptop.
The screen's blue glow hurt my eyes.
I typed: metformin side effects
The search results loaded.
My chest tightened.
Common side effects: Diarrhea. Nausea. Stomach cramping.
Serious side effects: Lactic acidosis. Kidney problems. Vitamin B12 deficiency.
I clicked the first result. Medical journal. Clinical study.
"Metformin-induced diarrhea affects 20-30% of patients. Typically develops within 1-2 weeks of initiating therapy. Diarrhea is chronic, persistent, debilitating. May require discontinuation."
Thirty percent.
I searched again: metformin kidney damage
Article after article.
"Long-term metformin use associated with progressive decline in renal function in susceptible patients..."
"Metformin-induced kidney injury can occur months to years after initiation..."
"Monitor creatinine and B12 levels regularly..."
My father's face flashed in my mind. The dialysis center. Three times a week. Four hours per session. For two years before his heart gave out.
I searched: metformin lactic acidosis
Images loaded.
Hospital beds. Ventilators. Emergency rooms.
One caption: "62-year-old female. Metformin-induced lactic acidosis after 3 years of therapy. Required emergency intubation."
Another: "Metformin lactic acidosis can occur at any time during therapy - even after years of use without incident."
A forum post: "My wife died from Metformin. Lactic acidosis. At the hospital. Age 54. No warning. Just... gone."
My heart hammered against my ribs. I closed the laptop. Rubbed my face with both hands.
What do I do?
The prescription sat on the counter. Five feet away. Mocking me.
I didn't fill it.
Three days passed.
The doctor's office called. "Ms. Mitchell, you haven't picked up your prescription. Dr. Chen needs confirmation you're taking the medication."
"I need more time."
"Ma'am, your A1C is 8.2. This is urgent. Dr. Chen was very clear - "
"I said I need more time."
I hung up.
Five days.
Seven.
My husband found me in the garage one evening. "Sandra. What are you doing out here?"
"Thinking."
"About?"
"Options."
"The doctor said you need medication."
"The doctor said my father needed medication too. Didn't save him. Just made his last eleven years unbearable."
His chin trembled. "But what if she's right? What if your blood sugar gets worse? What if I lose you?"
"What if the medication destroys my kidneys like it did his? What if I end up on dialysis? What if I die anyway but only after years of suffering?"
He had no answer.
That weekend I searched everything. Natural alternatives. Clinical studies. Research papers.
Oolong tea appeared everywhere. Natural antioxidants. EGCG and polyphenols. Studies from Duke, Stanford, Johns Hopkins showing blood sugar reductions.
Real universities. Real science. Not fringe pseudoscience.
Monday morning I ordered some oolong tea. Highest rated on Amazon. 4.3 stars. Over 8,000 reviews.
Seven weeks later: A1C still 8.1.
I tried another brand next. The one from the TV commercials. Nine weeks. Never missed a day.
A1C 7.9. Still diabetic range.
My follow-up appointment was in three weeks. Then two. Then one.
Every time I felt dizzy - reaching for something overhead, climbing stairs - I saw my father. The dialysis chair. The diarrhea that never stopped. The stomach cramps that one terrifying night at the hospital.
Ten days before my appointment, I stood in Whole Foods. Supplement aisle. Thirty different tea products.
All useless.
Two women talking one aisle over.
"-problem isn't oolong tea. Most brands destroy the antioxidants with heat processing. You need cold-extraction."
I walked over. "What did you say about heat destroying antioxidants?"
The older woman turned. Name badge: "Clinical Nutritionist."
"High-heat spray drying - cheap and fast. Destroys 90% of the EGCG and polyphenols that actually lower blood sugar."
My chest tightened. "I've been drinking oolong for four months. Numbers haven't moved."
"The clinical studies used whole leaf, high-altitude oolong. Most brands contain tea dust and fillers."
"The label doesn't say that."
"They don't have to disclose processing methods. Just 'oolong tea.'" She pulled out her phone. "Only one brand I recommend. PiPi Tea. Cold-extracted. High-altitude. Whole leaf. Published test results. Made in the USA."
Certificate of Analysis. Lab testing. Exact antioxidant content verified.
"How do I know it works? I'm out of time."
"Within 15-20 minutes you'll feel an energy lift. Proof it's hitting your bloodstream. Then over 2-4 weeks, blood sugar drops. You'll know immediately."
I pulled out my phone. Ordered it standing there.
The package arrived two days later.
I made the first cup that evening. Sat on the deck. Waited.
Seventeen minutes.
Then -
A lift. Like someone turned up the oxygen in my blood. The fog in my head... cleared. The exhaustion that hit me every afternoon around 3 PM... didn't come.
I walked inside. Grabbed the glucose meter from the bathroom.
Sat at the kitchen table. Pricked my finger. Checked the reading.
180.
I stared. Checked again.
180.
Down from 240.
It's working.
One week: 165.
I checked it morning, afternoon, evening. Numbers stayed consistent.
My husband noticed I stopped crashing after meals. Didn't comment. Just watched me move around with energy I hadn't had in months.
Two weeks: 155.
Three weeks: 145.
I called my sister one evening. Her blood sugar had been creeping up too.
"150 in the morning," I told her.
Silence on the other end.
"Sandra... how?"
I explained everything. The cold extraction. The whole leaf processing. The Certificate of Analysis. The published test results. The difference between processed garbage and the real thing.
"I'm sending you some," I said. "Your numbers were 220 last month. Try it."
Her voice cracked. "If this works - if you don't have to go through what Dad went through - "
"It's working. I promise."
The morning of my follow-up, I checked one last time: 142.
At the doctor's office, the nurse drew blood. Sent it to the lab. We waited.
She frowned at the results.
Drew blood again.
Sent it to a different lab.
"A1C 6.8."
Silence.
Dr. Chen pulled up my history. Stared at the numbers. Looked at me.
"Sandra. What happened?"
I told her. Cold-extracted oolong tea. Whole leaf. High-altitude. Third-party verified. Published test results. Made in the USA.
She typed notes. Nodding.
"Well." She closed the laptop. "Whatever you're doing, continue. These numbers are excellent. No Metformin necessary at this time."
No Metformin necessary.
I walked to my car. Got in. Sat there. Then called my husband.
"A1C 6.8."
I heard his breath catch. Then a sob.
"Thank God. Thank God, Sandra."
That was nine weeks ago.
My A1C this morning? 6.2.
Normal. Healthy. No medication. No diarrhea. No nausea. No kidney function decline. No lactic acidosis risk. No dialysis. No years of suffering while slowly dying anyway.
I'm not following my father's path.
Yesterday I hiked with my grandson for two hours. Full trail. Climbing. Walking. Not even winded afterward.
He grabbed me in a hug when we finished. "Grandma! That was awesome! Can we do this every weekend?"
My throat tightened. My eyes burned.
Because the answer was yes.

Your blood sugar's in the danger zone.

RESEP PLUM GLAZED STEAK WITH RICE
Bahan:
- 500 gr Beef
Bumbu Marinasi :
- 150 ml Juice Pear Korea
- 3 sdm Lee Kum Kee Kecap Asin Premium
- 1 sdm Lee Kum Kee Saus Plum
- 15 gr Lee Kum Kee Minyak Wijen Murni
- 35 gr Ginger
- 20 gr Garlic
- 1 sdt Lada Hitam
- 10 gr Chili Flake
- 35 gr Sugar
- 1 sdt Baking Powder
Saute veggie :
- 3 sdm Red Paprika
- 3 sdm Yellow Paprika
- 2 sdm Bawang Bombay
- 1 helai Daun Bawang
- 2 sdt Garlic
- 1 sdm Lee Kum Kee Kecap Asin Premium
- 1 sdm Lee Kum Kee Saus Plum
- Lada Putih
Sauce :
- 2 sdm Air Matang
- 1 sdm Lee Kum Kee Saus Plum
- 1 sdm Lee Kum Kee Kecap Asin Premium
- 1 sdm Lee Kum Kee Minyak Wijen Murni
Cara Membuat :
1. Campur semua bahan bumbu marinasi, aduk rata, marinasi beef selama minimum 40 menit atau semalaman.
2. Panaskan minyak goreng, tumis bawang bombay, paprika, dan daun bawang. Tambahkan Lee Kum Kee Kecap Asin Premium dan Lee Kum Kee Saus Plum, tumis sebentar, sajikan di atas piring saji.
3. Grill Beef dengan 2 pcs bawang, masak sampai tingkat kematangan sesuai yang kalian mau. Sajikan di piring saji.
4. Di pan yang sama, tambahkan air, lalu masukkan Lee Kum Kee Saus Plum dan Lee Kum Kee Kecap Asin Premium dan Lee Kum Kee Minyak Wijen Murni.
5. Siram saus di atas beef sajikan juga dengan nasi.
